points.description: Role of the learning rate: it controls the step size / speed of convergence of steepest descent. Low rate gives slow (overdamped) convergence; high rate gives faster but oscillating/zigzagging (underdamped) convergence.
points.partial_credit: Half if only says it controls speed/step size without describing the effect of low or high values, or gives only one of the low/high effects vaguely.

points.description: Danger: if the learning rate exceeds a critical value, learning becomes unstable (diverges rather than converges).
points.partial_credit: Half if only mentions oscillation/zigzagging or overshooting for a large rate without stating instability/divergence.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both: the learning rate sets step size/speed of convergence (with low = slow, high = oscillating), and the danger that too large a rate (above a critical value) makes learning unstable/diverge. Give half for vague or incomplete versions of either idea, e.g. only 'too large is bad' or only zigzagging. Give nothing for wrong or unrelated statements, such as saying a higher rate always improves learning.
